sermon.title: Build the Church Part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through the opening of 1 Corinthians to show what a young church possessed: holiness, calling on and summoning Jesus, grace as divine enablement, understanding of Scripture, stability, the gifts of the Spirit, looking for His coming, and fellowship with Christ. He contrasts this with the American church and urges believers to start the year seeing the Word of God as bigger than the opposition.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: he says “Matthew 13:12” for the words about brother betraying brother; those words are in Matthew 10:21 (the page shows Matthew 10:21, the passage that follows Matthew 10:17). The caption has the name of the man beaten before the court as “sanes”; it is written “Sosthenes” (1 Corinthians 1:1; Acts 18:17). The caption “starts beating” (paragraph starting at 14:08) may be a slip for “stops beating”; the words are left as spoken. “[Unclear]” marks two spots where the captions were not clear (in the paragraphs starting at 2:05 and 11:45).

chunks.section_question: Will following Jesus bring persecution, even from people close to you?
chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus warned, “Beware of men, for they will deliver you up to the councils,” and that they will “beat you in their synagogues” and bring you before governors and kings “for My sake.” He adds that brother will betray brother, and father the son.
chunks.text: Paul stayed a good while before leaving. So he was there a year and a half, and then a good while. We don’t know what the good while is, but the way I said it, it couldn’t be no more than three years. It could have been a lot less; could have been two and a half years. “Beware of men, for they will deliver you up to the councils,” Jesus said in Matthew 10:17. “They’ll beat you in their synagogues. They’ll bring you before governors and kings for My sake,” because you’re living for Me, because you’re proclaiming Me, “for a testimony against them,” and a testimony against nonbelievers. Unbelievers. He says in Matthew 13:12, “Brother shall betray brother to death, father the son, and children—their parents.”

chunks.section_question: Can you live for Christ on behalf of your children or spouse?
chunks.short_answer: He says parents cannot live for Christ for their children: “God doesn’t have any stepchildren,” and each adult child has to decide to live for Him. He says a spouse may go another way too, and believers must “stick with the Bible” and not water everything down.
chunks.text: Parents, you know, you can’t get down in the dumps because your kid decides to go sin after you raised him in a Christian school and in a Christian home and all the rest. They become an adult, they got to choose for themselves what road they’re going to take. Your job is to get them there; their job is to take the baton and live for Him. God doesn’t have any stepchildren. You can’t live for Christ for your children; they got to decide to live for Him themselves. Your spouse may decide to go another way, and it’s happening in America, isn’t it? They want to twist who God is and who Jesus is, and they want to water everything down, and they want you to accept them with their own beliefs, and you can’t do it, because you can’t change the Bible. You got to stick with the Bible. Can I hear an amen?

He happened to hit me and my family. Sometimes it’s health, sometimes it’s, uh, position, sometimes it’s, uh, money. You know, it just seems like you can’t keep a steady job.

chunks.text: You know, you got to rise above these things that Satan tries to distract you with and stay consistent. Now here is Paul training a new church. We jump over to 1 Corinthians. He writes a letter to them later. You see, a little bit later he writes back to this church and gives them instruction. Wow. And I want you to see right quick here the powerful statements he makes about this new church. And, folks, God is not a what? Respecter of persons. If He will do this for the Corinthian church, will He do it for all churches? Absolutely. Watch how he writes to these people. I mean, something happened in Corinth. chunks.section_question: What does it mean to be sanctified, holy and “called to be saints”?
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul did not say the Corinthians were going to be holy, but that “they are,” set apart for holiness and right living after turning from their sins. “Called to be saints” means morally blameless, which they were not yet, but they were “shooting for that mark.”
chunks.text:
Ready? “Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother.” Remember who got beat in front of the court? Sosthenes. Here he’s helping write this, uh, letter, this book. Hallelujah. See, his beating, his persecution, didn’t change him at all. He’s still with Paul, he’s still in the church, he’s still communicating, serving God. And number one: “to the church of God at Corinth, to them that are” what? Sanctified. They’re holy. He said, didn’t say they’re going to be holy; they are. What? Holy. Set apart for holiness, right living. They turn from their sins, their prostitution, their, their homosexuality, their lying, and their stealing, and all these things they had experienced.

Holiness. Isn’t that good? Look at the next one: “called to be saints.” You see, saints are blameless people. People that are blameless morally. Blameless. Now they’re called to be morally blameless, so obviously they’re not quite morally blameless yet. Ain’t that right? But they are what? Shooting for that mark. Isn’t that powerful? This church is not even three years old, and they’re experiencing things in God. “And in every place,” with all that, “in every place call upon the name of Jesus Christ.” Okay, so they’re calling on the name of Jesus Christ. Now that word “calling” means this: it’s not just inviting, or invoking, or hollering. It is summoning.

chunks.section_question: What does it mean to “call on the name of Jesus Christ” in church?
chunks.short_answer: He says “calling on the name of Jesus Christ” means summoning, like a court summons: “Can you send a substitute? No.” These believers summoned His presence, expecting and demanding that Jesus be there, while many people “go to church and never touch Jesus.”
chunks.text:
See, it’s acquiring. When you get a court summons, do you go? Yes. Can you send a substitute? No. Can you say, “I’m too busy, excuse me”? No, you ought to appear. Then see, what is he saying? These people summon Jesus Christ. They summon His presence. He appears in their midst, not by the physical eye, but His presence touching our presence, our spirit. Amen. Do you see that? Now see, these are things this young church were possessing. When they come together, they were expecting, they were demanding, that Jesus Christ be there, like He said, “If two or three are gathered together, I will be” where? “In the midst.” They summoned Him.

And so many people go to church and never touch Jesus, but yet this Corinthian church were touching Him. They were summoning Him. Isn’t that beautiful? I think that’s tremendous. Folks, I mean, our mega churches today don’t have anything like this. We’ve gotten off of these basic things. Now remember, these are ex-prostitutes, homosexuals, idolaters, gamblers, Jews, non-Jews, slaves, slave masters, sailors, merchants, soldiers, drunkards, contractors, athletes and entertainers. They were all coming to Christ: different races, different nationalities, different cultures.

chunks.section_question: What is grace? Is it just God’s favor?
chunks.short_answer: He says grace is more than “just favor”: it shows in “the divine influence upon your life, divine enablement to live a lifestyle different than you lived before.” He says the American church has done members “a disservice” by teaching that God favors you no matter what you do.
chunks.text: Verse three of 1 Corinthians 1: “Grace be to you and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ. I thank my God always on your behalf for the grace of God given you by Jesus Christ.” And this is where the American church has done the church members a disservice. They keep telling them grace is just favor, God just favors you no matter what you do, He favors you. But it’s much more than that. He favors you, and it shows in a result of the divine influence upon your life, divine enablement to live a lifestyle different than you lived before. That’s the full measure of grace. That’s the whole purpose of grace: that He favors you, He loves you, He’s going to work with you so that people will see that there’s a divine influence, a divine enablement, that changed your life from this way to His way.

chunks.section_question: What does it mean to be “confirmed” and stable in Christ?
chunks.short_answer: He says “confirm” means “stable, unchanging,” and that the young Corinthian Christians might make a mistake but “got back up and kept moving forward.” He says the American church has a lot of “instability,” with people who can’t overcome alcohol, drugs or anger because they are not experiencing these things.
chunks.text: Amen. That’s what God says He wants us to know: the Scriptures, that way we can what? Speak it. And that makes us wealthy. That’s the true wealth of the church. “Even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you.” That word “confirm” is to be stable, unchanging. These young Christians were stable. They weren’t going in and out, up and down. They were unchanging. They might make a mistake here and there, but they got back up and kept moving forward. How many would like to be stable in God? Now, in the American church, we got a lot of instability. We got big buildings, and we got great authors, and book authors, and preachers, and everything else, and God’s people can’t handle the slightest tribulation or problems in their life. They can’t overcome alcohol, they can’t overcome drugs, they can’t overcome anger, they ain’t going to overcome nothing. Why? Because they’re not experiencing these things.

chunks.section_question: What does it mean to look for the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ?
chunks.short_answer: He says looking for the coming of the Lord means being faithful and wise, thinking, living and talking with superiority, because you may meet Him when you die and don’t have to “wait for the rapture.” He cites Matthew 24:46 and says Jesus told them to “watch, be ready.”
chunks.text:
“And the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.” You say, “Oh, big deal, the coming of the Lord.” Well, you got to understand what he means by the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ. Well, I know what it means: He’s coming again. That’s right, but you got to understand your part in it. See, how are you supposed to think about the coming of the Lord? These guys were looking for the coming, and Jesus wasn’t coming for 2,000 years down the road or more, but they’re what? Looking. They’re what? Looking. And don’t you believe these people to tell you. See, they didn’t even understand. They thought He was coming in, you know, right then and during their lifetime. That does not mean that at all. Let me show you what it means. Are you ready for this?

Matthew 24:46: “Blessed is he that is faithful and a wise servant, whom his master, when he comes, will find so doing.” Doing what? Being wise and faithful, ain’t that right? So they’re looking for the coming of Christ. What does that mean? They’re being faithful, and they’re talking with superiority, thinking with superiority, and living a superior life. Remember what wisdom was in Proverbs: superior thinking, superior living, and superior talking. Why? Because He can come and take you. You can die, you know. You don’t have to wait for the rapture. You’re going to meet Him when your heart starts beating. So you should be what? Faithful, and you should be a wise servant.

So see, when we’re saying we’re looking for Christ’s return, we’re saying what? I am faithful, I am living a wise life, I am speaking wisely, I am thinking wisely, because Christ may show up, or I may die and I will appear before Him. So it’s a lifestyle. And this is what Jesus told them to do: watch, be ready.

chunks.short_answer: He says, “It doesn’t matter if He comes in your lifetime or not.” God will make them stable and unchanging to the end and keep them blameless, which he defines as “unaccusable” in the day of the Lord Jesus Christ, because Christ will finish the good work He began.

Stable, unchanging. See, He’s going to confirm you, make you stable, unchanging, and to the end. What’s the end? That day when He comes the second time and judges the world, “that you may be blameless.” And what’s blameless? Unaccusable. “In the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.” How many of you want to be unaccusable in the day of the Lord Jesus Christ? How many? You know, this Corinthian church is on its way. It’s sanctified, it’s calling on the Lord, summoning Him, it’s looking for the return of Christ, they have the gifts of the Spirit working in the church. I mean, isn’t this beautiful? They are stable, they’re unchanging, they might make some mistakes, they are saints that are looking forward to being blameless, knowing that Christ will finish the good work that He began in us, and on that day they will be blameless.

scriptures.text_nkjv: who will also confirm you to the end, that you may be blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

chunks.section_question: What is the “fellowship” of God’s Son, and what is eternal life?
chunks.short_answer: He says the last thing the Corinthians had was “the fellowship of His Son”: not a ministry or church group but “an intimate relationship with Christ.” He cites John 17:3 and defines eternal life as “knowing God and Jesus Christ,” not “head knowledge.”
chunks.text:
Hallelujah. Ain’t that powerful? Now, senior saints, he did this with five people in his team. We got more than five here this morning. We got a head start. Verse 9: “God is faithful, by whom we were called unto the” what? “Fellowship.” Here’s the last one. See, “the fellowship of His Son.” Not some ministry, not some church group. These guys are in partnership with Jesus Christ. Not Paul, not Aquila, not Priscilla, not Silas, not Timothy. They are in partnership with Christ. They are in an intimate relationship with Christ. This is the biggest thing these guys had: they actually know Him.

How, you know, that makes a difference. Not head knowledge. This is a real possession of Christ, a fellowship, a partnership with Him. It says in John 17:3, “This is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.” Definition of eternal life is what? Knowing God and Jesus Christ, an intimate relationship. The Bible says that Joseph knew not Mary until after Jesus was born; in other words, he didn’t have an intimate relationship with Mary. And see, we have this intimacy with God. We know God, we fellowship with Him, we partner with Him. We’re not partnered with just Silas and Timothy and Paul. We’re partnered with Jesus Himself, and that makes the difference.

and did not know her till she had brought forth her firstborn Son. And he called His name JESUS.

chunks.section_question: How do we know that we know Jesus?
chunks.short_answer: He cites 1 John 2:3, “We know that we know Him if we keep His commandments,” and says it is imperative that people meet and know Jesus in their salvation. “It’s not the baptismal certificate, it’s not what church you belong to, it’s who you know.”
chunks.text: 1 John 2:3: “We know that we know Him if we keep His commandments.” See, “He that says, ‘I know Him,’ and keeps them not is a liar, and the truth is not in him.” So is it imperative, very important, that people in their salvation meet and know Jesus Christ? Yes. It’s not the baptismal certificate, it’s not what church you belong to, it’s who you know. And this is what changed the Corinthians in this wild, wild city that any normal modern ministry would look at and go, “This city is impossible.” And yet the Word of God changed these people’s lives, and they knew Him. They encountered Christ.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now by this we know that we know Him, if we keep His commandments. He who says, “I know Him,” and does not keep His commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.

chunks.section_question: How should Christians face a new year, and will the nations worship?
chunks.short_answer: He says to “stop looking at all the opposition and the problems” and see that the Word of God is bigger than this world. He closes with the overcomers’ song in Revelation 15, where “all nations shall come,” and says “shall” means it is impossible for it not to happen.
chunks.text:
Hallelujah. Now, we got a year ahead of us, and we got to start looking and seeing like Paul looked and saw. Amen. We got to stop looking at all the opposition and the problems and see that the Word of God is bigger than this world. It’s bigger than anybody’s lack of faith, or whatever. Now, I chose Revelation 15:3 because the verse before this says, “These that overcame the beast,” they that overcame his mark, the number of his name, and his image. And in Revelation 12, the same people overcame Satan by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony, and loved not their life to death. These people who what? Overcame.

Then these people sang the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying, “great and marvelous”—why, there’s, they’re overcomers, they’re seeing the good stuff, “great and marvelous are Thy works, Lord God Almighty, just and true are Your ways, You King of saints. Who shall not fear You, O Lord, and honor Your name? For You only are holy, and all nations shall come.” That word “shall” means it is impossible for it not to happen. “They will come and worship before You,” whether they believe in You or not, they’re going to come. But we want to be like Paul, to get the nations to come and worship Him because they accept Him, amen, and not reject Him.

faqs.question: How long did Paul stay at Corinth?
faqs.answer: He says Paul stayed “a year and a half, and then a good while.” He says nobody knows what the good while is, but the way he said it, it couldn’t be no more than three years and could have been two and a half.

scriptures.text_nkjv: So Paul still remained a good while. Then he took leave of the brethren and sailed for Syria, and Priscilla and Aquila were with him. He had his hair cut off at Cenchrea, for he had taken a vow.

faqs.question: What should parents do when a grown child chooses sin after a Christian upbringing?
faqs.answer: He says parents can’t “get down in the dumps”: “Your job is to get them there; their job is to take the baton and live for Him.” He says you can’t live for Christ for your children; they have to decide to live for Him themselves.

faqs.question: Will God do for churches today what He did for the church at Corinth?
faqs.answer: He asks, “If He will do this for the Corinthian church, will He do it for all churches? Absolutely.” He says something happened in Corinth that is not like the mega churches of today.

faqs.question: What does he say about the man who was beaten in front of the court and is named in 1 Corinthians 1:1?
faqs.answer: He says his beating and persecution “didn’t change him at all”: he is still with Paul, in the church, communicating and serving God, and is helping write the letter.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother,

faqs.question: Were the Corinthians already holy, or just going to be?
faqs.answer: He says the verse does not say they are going to be holy; “they are.” He explains holy as set apart for holiness and right living, since they had turned from their sins and the things they had experienced.

scriptures.text_nkjv: To the church of God which is at Corinth, to those who are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, with all who in every place call on the name of Jesus Christ our Lord, both theirs and ours:

faqs.question: Why does he compare calling on Jesus to a court summons?
faqs.answer: He says when you get a court summons you go, you can’t send a substitute and you can’t say you’re too busy. In the same way, the Corinthians summoned His presence and He appeared in their midst, “not by the physical eye,” but touching “our spirit.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For where two or three are gathered together in My name, I am there in the midst of them.”

faqs.question: What kinds of people made up the Corinthian church?
faqs.answer: He lists ex-prostitutes, homosexuals, idolaters, gamblers, Jews, non-Jews, slaves, slave masters, sailors, merchants, soldiers, drunkards, contractors, athletes and entertainers. He says they were “all coming to Christ: different races, different nationalities, different cultures.”

faqs.question: What does he say is the full measure of grace?
faqs.answer: He says it is not only that God favors and loves you but that He is going to work with you so that people will see “a divine influence, a divine enablement, that changed your life.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: I thank my God always concerning you for the grace of God which was given to you by Christ Jesus,

faqs.question: Why does he say the American church has a lot of instability?
faqs.answer: He says there are big buildings, authors and preachers, but God’s people “can’t handle the slightest tribulation or problems in their life.” They can’t overcome alcohol, drugs or anger, he says, “because they’re not experiencing these things.”

faqs.question: Which spiritual gifts does he say American churches usually express?
faqs.answer: He says an American church usually has “one gift expressed”: in certain circles prophecy, in others tongues, in others healing, and in other circles “nothing.” He says the Corinthians lacked none of the gifts when the church came together.

scriptures.text_nkjv: so that you come short in no gift, eagerly waiting for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,

faqs.question: Do you have to wait for the rapture to meet Jesus?
faqs.answer: He says “you don’t have to wait for the rapture,” because you can die and appear before Him. So he says you should be faithful and a wise servant now.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Blessed is that servant whom his master, when he comes, will find so doing.

faqs.question: What does he say “watch, be ready” means?
faqs.answer: He says it is a lifestyle: “I am faithful, I am living a wise life, I am speaking wisely, I am thinking wisely,” because Christ may show up or you may die and appear before Him. He says it is “the attitude” and “the motive of your heart.”

faqs.question: Does a baptismal certificate or church membership make you right with God?
faqs.answer: He says, “It’s not the baptismal certificate, it’s not what church you belong to, it’s who you know.” He says it is imperative that people in their salvation meet and know Jesus Christ.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now by this we know that we know Him, if we keep His commandments. He who says, “I know Him,” and does not keep His commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.

faqs.question: What does he say about the overcomers’ song in Revelation 15?
faqs.answer: He says the people who overcame sang the song of Moses and the song of the Lamb: “great and marvelous are Thy works.” He says “all nations shall come” means it is impossible for it not to happen, and that they will come and worship whether they believe or not.
